title: The Unexpected Locker
premise: Marguerite Crane, seventeen, has spent years cooking, chauffeuring, and covering for his three younger siblings while their mother works hospital night shifts—counting down to graduation as his only escape. Cleaning out their late grandmother's kitchen, he finds a recipe box whose cards hold coded instructions to a hidden community theater troupe Grandma secretly ran for decades. Drawn into its orbit—and into a slow-burn romance with stage manager Theo—Marguerite must choose between the duty-label of 'parent' everyone pinned on him and the self he's never allowed on stage. When Mom discovers the truth the week of the final audition, he learns that belonging isn't abandoning family but letting them see him whole; the book ends with him taking his bow as both brother and himself.
about_author: Edmund Sterling is a former high school drama teacher who writes quiet, hopeful stories about kids who grow up too fast. He lives in a small river town with his partner and an opinionated cat named Encore.

chapters.title: Sixty-Two Days
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A morning montage of packing lunches, forging mom's signature, and counting days to graduation establishes his invisible caretaker role and resentment simmering under love. Emotional beat: exhaustion disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Box That Doesn't Smell Like Cinnamon
chapters.summary: While clearing Grandma's old kitchen for a landlord inspection, Marguerite finds recipe cards with stage directions instead of measurements. His little sister Junie catches him reading one aloud. POV: Marguerite. Beat: first crack of curiosity in his routine.

chapters.title: Card Number Seven
chapters.summary: Following a card's directions leads to the shuttered Orpheum annex, where a ragtag community troupe rehearses—Grandma's old company, still waiting on 'Maggie's kid.' Theo, the wry stage manager, hands him a broom instead of a welcome. POV: Marguerite. Beat: reluctant intrigue.

chapters.title: Cover Story
chapters.summary: Marguerite lies to Mom about study group, juggles siblings and secret rehearsals, and nearly gets caught when youngest brother Devi has a meltdown at pickup. Theo covers for him without judgment. POV: alternating Marguerite/Devi. Beat: guilt entangling with belonging.

chapters.title: Understudy
chapters.summary: A lead actor drops out; the director pushes Marguerite onstage despite his protests. Rehearsals become the one hour a day he isn't needed. First almost-kiss with Theo after lights-out. POV: Marguerite. Beat: terrifying joy.

chapters.title: What Junie Knew
chapters.summary: Junie reveals she found the box weeks ago and has been leaving cards where he'd find them—she wanted him back. Sibling fight turns tender; they agree to keep the secret together. POV: Junie. Beat: found family reframes blood family.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Mom comes home early, hollowed out by a brutal shift, and finds the playbill in Marguerite's backpack. She accuses him of abandoning them like Grandma did. POV: Mom. Beat: duty weaponized; the label 'parent' made explicit.

chapters.title: Cards on the Table
chapters.summary: Mom reads the full recipe box and discovers Grandma's letters: she chose theater over respectability and regretted hiding it, not choosing it. Mother and son argue toward honesty about money, sacrifice, and who owes whom a life. POV: alternating. Beat: rising tension peaks offstage.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Opening night collides with Devi's school crisis; the siblings rally so Marguerite can perform, proving care can be shared rather than carried alone. He steps into the light as himself, Theo watching from the wings. POV: Marguerite. Beat: climax—love against duty resolved into love through duty.

chapters.title: Encore, With Extra Butter
chapters.summary: Weeks later: Mom takes a day-shift schedule, the Cranes attend Sunday matinees together, and Marguerite writes his own card for the box—a recipe for staying visible. Graduation arrives and feels like a beginning. POV: Marguerite. Beat: belonging earned, labels off.
